Foundation 21: CNA::Runtime::BclProjection is the measured register of non-XNA CLR identities this binding projects — System.EventArgs to CNA::Runtime::EventArgs, and System.Exception and System.Runtime.InteropServices.ExternalException to the Ruby StandardError root. The API verifier resolves and shape-checks every entry under LANGUAGE_MAPPING_MISMATCH and the dependency frontier consumes the same register, so no BCL type can be reported as mapped that the runtime does not project. StandardError rather than ::Exception because a CLR catch (Exception) is the analogue of a bare Ruby rescue; an intermediate BCL exception class the XNA surface never names collapses to the nearest projected ancestor. System.Type, IServiceProvider, IO.Stream, TimeSpan as a first-class type, Attribute, StringBuilder, SerializationInfo, ReadOnlyCollection and Dictionary are deliberately not designed

Foundation 22: six XNA exception types as real Ruby exceptions rooted at StandardError - Audio InstancePlayLimitException, NoAudioHardwareException, NoMicrophoneConnectedException; Graphics DeviceLostException, DeviceNotResetException, NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException; 6 types / 18 Ruby identities. The pinned IL shows all eight XNA exception types declare zero fields, zero methods and four constructors whose entire body is a pure forward to the CLR exception base, with no message synthesis and no validation. The inner exception maps to Ruby Exception#cause, bound at construction with the backtrace cleared, so an unraised exception matches the CLR's InnerException set and StackTrace null. ContentLoadException and StorageDeviceNotConnectedException stay deferred on System.Runtime.Serialization. Nothing in this binding raises any of them, and no audio engine, Content or Storage namespace is added

No Microsoft-owned bytes and no machine-local path is committed, and the gem packages zero Microsoft binaries
